- Overestimate prices when sentiment is positive (especially >0.3) and recent history shows upward momentum.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative or neutral (especially <0.2) and recent prices are trending down.
- Overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., >78) — model tends to overreact and peak too high, then corrects.
- Lag in response to sentiment shifts — model reacts 1–2 days after sentiment changes, especially when sentiment turns bullish.
- Mean reversion bias: model often holds prices too high in strong bullish sentiment, then underestimates correction.
- For 30-day forecasts, avoid assuming linear continuation — sentiment and recent volatility should trigger early mean-reversion adjustments.
- When sentiment is high and price is near 78–80, reduce forecast by 1–2 points to avoid overconfidence in momentum.
- If sentiment is low and price is near 75–76, increase forecast slightly to avoid underestimating support.
